learning: Across iterations 6 to 10, no geometry or controller change beat 70.83 at 12 mm footprints with ±0.03 m span. Mass at its 0.4 kg floor was the only single change that raised the score in isolation. The one-per-run line loss on the s-bend and slalom persisted under every geometry change tested.
notes: Final-iteration package: the iteration 6 geometry and the iteration 6 controller, unchanged. This is the design with two confirmed scores of 70.83, so no untested lever is added before the unseen-track race.
rationale: The iteration 6 geometry (mass 0.4 kg, body 0.16 m by 0.12 m, five 12 mm sensors at x = +0.03, +0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03 and y = 0.05 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m) has the best evidence: 70.83 in iterations 6 and 10. Every other geometry change tested since then lowered the score or left line losses at 1.0 per run (y 0.07 m, body_length 0.12 m, 8 mm footprints, the ±0.04 m span at 36.6, and wheel_track 0.14 m at 69.05). I keep that geometry unchanged. The controller is also kept exactly as in iteration 6 (kp 3.0, ki 0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.5, last_direction line loss, weights +1, +0.5, 0, -0.5, -1). The only controller change ever tried (iteration 1, kp 4.5 and kd 0.3 on a narrower track) was confounded and scored 53.7. The controller is the only variable left on the unseen track, and an untested gain change could not be checked by any later race, so I do not add one. Expected result, as a prediction only: a score near 70.8 on the development tracks, with about one line loss per run on the s-bend and slalom.
